work_order.understanding: Not a council run in substance: plan/critique.json is an empty object, so there was no critique to judge, apply or dismiss. I did that reading myself against the code, and the proposal's load-bearing claims held. Issue #22 is a React validateDOMNesting warning on /reports: on main, ReportCard.tsx:108-127 wraps every dashboard widget body in the component library's <Button variant="bare">, and Button.tsx:166-178 renders react-aria-components' ReactAriaButton with only a className and no element-type override, so it always emits a real <button>. CalendarCard's month-name Button is the body that nests today, but the wrapper is the fault and the one change corrects every body. The open PR #26 already swapped that wrapper for <View role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick onKeyDown>, but its keydown handler has no e.repeat guard and no e.target check: holding Space pushed one history entry per auto-repeat (BUG-002), and because preventDefault ran before any target check it also suppressed a descendant control's browser-synthesized click, leaving that control keyboard-dead. Two things ride along. First, useDashboardWidget.ts:17 and useReport.ts:9 declare queries `enabled: !!id && !!type` / `enabled: !!id`; a disabled react-query v5 query reports status 'pending' indefinitely, and the components that destructure isPending (seven of twelve importers) plus CustomReport.tsx:122 all return <LoadingIndicator /> forever, so /reports/spending and bare /reports/custom spin. Second, AC-6 asked QA to compare against a base commit that no QA run can serve — the workflow checks out one ref and boots the app once from it — so it was unperformable and unpassable. This version restates it as absolute assertions and fixes the standing rejection's actual objection, which was correct: v6 asserted that a FinancialText-wrapped numeric cell computes pageText AND font-size 13px, naming CalendarCard, and that is unsatisfiable because every such figure sits under an ancestor that sets colour and/or font-size explicitly, so 13px and pageText never co-occur on one element in any widget body. AC-6 is therefore split per element, each half traced to the declaration that produces it: the card title <h2> is the colour probe, and the DateRange line beneath it is the font-size probe.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent product defects plus one defective criterion. (1) ReportCard.tsx:108-127 renders its children inside a literal <Button variant="bare"> whenever the card has a `to` route, is not editing and is not click-disabled; the component library's Button forwards to react-aria-components with no element override, so it always emits a <button> and any widget body containing a button nests button-in-button. (2) The replacement on origin/sdlc/issue-22 dropped press semantics the primitive owned: the hand-written onKeyDown has no e.repeat check and no e.target check, so one Space press navigates once per auto-repeat, and because it calls e.preventDefault() before any target check it also suppresses a descendant control's browser-synthesized click, leaving that control keyboard-dead. (3) useDashboardWidget.ts:17 and useReport.ts:9 declare queries whose enabled predicates go false when the id is absent; a disabled query stays 'pending' forever and every consuming component returns <LoadingIndicator /> indefinitely. (4) AC-6 asked QA to diff against a base commit that no QA run can serve, making it unperformable, and its replacement asserted a single element computes both pageText and 13px — a combination no element in any widget body satisfies — so it was unpassable too. AC-6 is now two per-element assertions, each expected value traced to the declaration that produces it.
work_order.approach: Three changes, all small, all at the shared layer. A) In ReportCard.tsx the clickable branch's final state is a <View role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick={goToReport} onKeyDown={...}> holding `content` — on main this replaces <Button variant="bare">, on the PR branch it already exists, so the entry states the end state rather than a diff. The keydown handler is ordered: return unless e.key is 'Enter' or ' '; return early if e.target !== e.currentTarget; call e.preventDefault(); return early if e.repeat; call goToReport(). The target check precedes preventDefault deliberately — the previous version called preventDefault first, which suppresses a native descendant control's synthesized click and swallows a space typed in any text field a widget body contains. Scoping preventDefault to the card still stops Space scrolling the page, because the first keydown of a press carries repeat: false. Keep activating on keydown so QA's measured timing does not shift. Do not switch to usePress: it commits Space on keyup, and no component under components/reports/ imports usePress or PressResponder today. Do not add aria-label and do not add a hover background. B) Leave geometry otherwise untouched — the body's backgroundColor, its boxShadow '0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.15)' and its ':hover' deepening to '0 4px 6px', the IntersectionObserver render gate, and the Layout wrapper. View's viewStyles and the old Button's defaultButtonClassName differ in flex properties, so AC-5's bounding-rect check is what verifies this does not move the card. C) Fix loading in the two shared hooks and nowhere else: hold the useQuery result, derive `const isFirstLoad = query.isPending && query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'`, return it under both isPending and isLoading. The conjunction is react-query v5's own isLoading definition and changes exactly one of the four query states — a disabled query. Do not derive from fetchStatus !== 'idle' alone: that is also true during a background refetch over cached data, which would blank every report route on every navigation and refocus. No queryKey, queryFn, select or enabled change in either hook, and no report component changes.

risks: The hook change alters a flag seven report routes read on isPending and five read on isLoading, and the widening adds /reports/custom. Checked call site by call site: every render-time read of `widget` is optional-chained (Crossover.tsx:132-141 reaches widget.meta! only inside a branch that already proved it defined; BudgetAnalysis.tsx:244-252 and Summary.tsx:88-90 are the same shape) and every save affordance sits behind `if (!widget) { throw ... }` or a `widget ?` / `widget &&` render guard, so no unguarded widget.id becomes reachable. Any report behaving differently after AC-2 passes is this change's doing.

Overriding both isPending and isLoading on a UseQueryResult is a deliberately unusual shape: callers destructuring either name get the useful answer, but anything reading the result generically would get the derived one. All twelve call sites destructure; no site reads the result object whole.

`isFirstLoad` uses the conjunction rather than fetchStatus !== 'idle' alone; the two differ only in the disabled case, where the conjunction is correct. The cached-background-refetch case in both hook test files is what pins this.

Making the click surface a View with role="button" rather than a real button trades native semantics for explicit ones, leaving a role=button wrapping real buttons and exposing two tab stops to the same destination; that trade-off predates this change and is listed in out_of_scope rather than silently inherited.

The e.target guard must come before e.preventDefault(). The recorded review finding is that preventDefault on a descendant control's keydown suppresses the browser-synthesized click, so the wrong order does not merely double-navigate — it makes the inner control keyboard-dead. The new test cases pin the order and use a native <button>, because the branch's existing inner-control cases use react-aria's Button, which stops propagation and therefore pass either way.

View's viewStyles and the removed Button's defaultButtonClassName disagree on flex properties, so the card body could in principle be laid out differently even though the body's own width and height are 100% in both worlds. AC-5's bounding-rect measurement is the check for this; if the rects disagree by more than 1px, that is the finding, not a rounding artefact.
